Fit each completed design

Source: R/mi.R
svysem.svyimputationList.Rd

svysem(), svycfa() and svygrowth() dispatch on a svyimputationList. Every completed design is passed to the same generic, which selects lavaan::sem(), lavaan::cfa() or lavaan::growth(). estimator may be "MLM", "WLSMV", or "MLR". parallel is any function of (X, FUN) with the same contract as lapply(); NULL uses lapply(). It loops imputations. Replicate weights inside one WLSMV fit stay sequential, so the two loops are not nested. Tests and examples use at most two cores.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'svyimputationList'
svysem(
  model,
  design,
  estimator = c("MLM", "WLSMV", "MLR"),
  replicates = NULL,
  replicate.type = NULL,
  parallel = NULL,
  ...,
  on_fail = c("stop", "omit")
)

# S3 method for class 'svyimputationList'
svycfa(
  model,
  design,
  estimator = c("MLM", "WLSMV", "MLR"),
  replicates = NULL,
  replicate.type = NULL,
  parallel = NULL,
  ...,
  on_fail = c("stop", "omit")
)

# S3 method for class 'svyimputationList'
svygrowth(
  model,
  design,
  estimator = c("MLM", "WLSMV", "MLR"),
  replicates = NULL,
  replicate.type = NULL,
  parallel = NULL,
  ...,
  on_fail = c("stop", "omit")
)

Arguments

model

Model syntax, as for lavaan::sem(), lavaan::cfa() or lavaan::growth().

design

A svyimputationList, from svydesign(data = mitools::imputationList(...)).

estimator

Variance estimator. "MLM", "WLSMV", or "MLR".

replicates, replicate.type

Passed to each completed design. See svysem(). Replicate weights inside an imputation are not parallelized.

parallel

NULL to use lapply(), or a function called as parallel(X, FUN). One example is function(X, FUN) parallel::mclapply(X, FUN, mc.cores = 2).

...

Passed to the fitter for each completed design.

on_fail

"stop" (default) or "omit". "omit" drops a failed imputation, records it in the status table, and continues.

Value

A svysem_mi object. Its df slot is the design degrees of freedom and is the default df.com for pooling.

References

Rubin D (1987). Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys. Wiley, New York. doi:10.1002/9780470316696

Barnard J, Rubin DB (1999). "Small-Sample Degrees of Freedom with Multiple Imputation." Biometrika, 86(4), 948–959. doi:10.1093/biomet/86.4.948

See also

pooled_estimates(), pooled_wald(), survey::svydesign()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("mitools", quietly = TRUE)) {
  base <- simulate_design(
    n_psu = 6, n_per = 4, n_strata = 2, seed = 1
  )$variables
  alt <- base
  alt$y <- alt$y + 0.2
  des <- survey::svydesign(
    ids = ~psu, strata = ~strat, weights = ~w,
    data = mitools::imputationList(list(base, alt))
  )
  fit <- svysem(
    "y ~ x1 + x2", des,
    fixed.x = FALSE, meanstructure = TRUE
  )
  coef(fit)
}
#>        y~x1        y~x2        y~~y      x1~~x1      x1~~x2      x2~~x2 
#>  0.44063045 -0.48330670  0.88005445  0.72560561 -0.08520233  0.95830528 
#>         y~1        x1~1        x2~1 
#>  1.00160774  0.08784715  0.10371083
